Plan Scope (_deprecations.py): 'state in the entry why this one is scheduled, or a later reader will assume it is a mistake.' — this is a developer-facing rationale comment, not the operator-facing warning text.

findings.finding: The deprecation warning message text — the operator-facing string emitted by `warn_deprecated` when `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is set — is never drafted in the plan. The plan specifies the mechanism (`warn_deprecated`, `_scheduled(...)` in REGISTRY) and says to annotate the entry for future developers, but does not specify what migration instruction an operator reads at runtime. An operator whose process emits the warning needs, in the message itself: (1) which variable is deprecated, (2) what class-config keys replace it, and (3) when it will be removed. Without a specified message, the AC that the warning is emitted via `warn_deprecated` can be satisfied by a message that contains none of those three elements, leaving operators with a warning they cannot act on.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC: 'a test asserts the deprecation warning is emitted when REBAR_LLM_MODEL is set, via warn_deprecated'
scenarios: Operator running `rebar review` in any supported shape (CLI, MCP, library) sees a deprecation warning with no migration instruction and cannot determine what `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]` keys to set instead — they are stuck until they find the ADR or docs, defeating the purpose of the per-call warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Warning message' subsection to Scope/_deprecations.py entry that drafts the text, e.g.: "REBAR_LLM_MODEL is deprecated and will be removed in v1.0.0. Set per-class env vars (REBAR_LLM_FAST_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_SMART_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_LONG_CONTEXT_MODEL) or use [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] in your config instead."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify and document (in the ADR or Scope) whether `warn_deprecated` bypasses Python's default per-location warning dedup (e.g., uses `logging`, calls `warnings.warn` with `stacklevel` that varies per call site, or resets filters) — if it uses `warnings.warn` with default filters, either accept the once-per-location semantics and update AC4 accordingly, or add explicit `warnings.simplefilter('always')` resets where needed.
evidence: Plan quote: 'warn_deprecated (`_deprecations.py:299-329`) emits UNCONDITIONALLY on every call — verified, there is no `_seen` set, no `_emitted` flag and no `warnings.warn` filter'

The plan's AC4 test requirement depends entirely on this assertion being true at runtime, not just at the source level — Python's default warnings filter suppresses repeated DeprecationWarning from the same (module, lineno) pair in a long-running process

The plan does not show or cite the actual `warn_deprecated` implementation body to confirm it bypasses or resets Python's filter machinery (e.g., via `warnings.warn(..., stacklevel=...)` with a unique stacklevel, `logging`-based emission, or a custom sink)
findings.finding: The plan asserts `warn_deprecated` (at `_deprecations.py:299-329`) emits unconditionally on every call with no dedup — 'verified, there is no `_seen` set, no `_emitted` flag and no `warnings.warn` filter'. This is a load-bearing capability assertion: if warn_deprecated actually wraps `warnings.warn` with the default Python filter (which suppresses duplicate DeprecationWarning from the same call site), the per-call emission guarantee the plan relies on would be silently violated in production. The plan's own AC4 test ('per call, not once-per-process') would pass in test but fail in a running process if Python's warning filter deduplication is in play.
findings.location: Testing section (AC4 / 'per call' requirement) and Scope → `src/rebar/_deprecations.py:299`
scenarios: A long-running worker process calls `load_class_slots()` repeatedly; if Python's default filter deduplicates by (module, lineno), operators only see the deprecation warning on first invocation — the plan's 'per call' contract is broken silently
AC4 passes in test (each test resets the warnings filter) but the assertion is vacuous about runtime behaviour
